unsigned: A credential without a proof asserts nothing; it is a JSON document with claims in it.
proof-in-wrong-domain: A proof made in the attestation domain must not be presentable as a credential proof, which is the whole purpose of domain separation.
no-agent-key: A credential that names an agent but not its key cannot be tied to anything the agent signs.
never-expires: An identity credential that never expires is one a verifier is never forced to re-check.
unknown-assurance-level: Assurance levels are a closed vocabulary; an unknown one would be read as 'higher than the highest' by a naive comparison.
